key_insight: Noise can disrupt ADAPT-VQE not only during parameter optimization but also during operator selection, and error mitigation can restore convergence.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum hardware, combining mitigation methods can make adaptive variational algorithms more robust and practically usable under realistic noise.
method: Tested ADAPT-VQE operator selection on linear H3 under multiple coherent and incoherent noise channels.
Applied dynamical decoupling, zero-noise extrapolation, and Pauli twirling, individually and in combination.
Compared convergence behavior across noise rates to assess resilience of the selection step.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that sufficiently high noise rates can prevent convergence, while appropriately combined mitigation techniques restore a successful convergence profile.
watch_item: Mitigation effectiveness may depend on noise strength, channel type, and how the techniques are combined, so the result may not transfer unchanged to all devices or ansätze.
paper_title: A Case Study on Noise Resilient Operator Selection in Adaptive Variational Quantum Algorithms
